subject: Blackout windows & credit ladder — proposed redline and legal handoff
messages:
From: Anna Ruiz <anna@helixlabs.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel@helixlabs.com>, Helix Labs Legal <legal@helixlabs.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft order form and SLA — blackout windows & credits

Jonas,

Thanks for sending the draft. Our legal team reviewed the MSA + order form and pushed back on the maintenance / blackout language and how credits scale for regional outages. Two quick asks from our side: 1) narrow the definition of a scheduled blackout so we can avoid surprise production slowness during weekday business hours, and 2) provide a clearer stepped credit ladder for partial regional degradation (we're trying to model this against our own customer SLAs).

I've attached Helix's annotated copy (helix_redline_v2.docx). Can you route to your legal and ops and let me know whether the deferral language is negotiable? We can be flexible on a small weekday maintenance window if we get stricter guardrails and an explicit patch rollback SLA.

Would prefer to have a redline back by Dec 19 so procurement can complete the PO before year end. Happy to hop on a 30-min call next week if that helps.

Thanks,
Anna Ruiz
Head of Platform Ops
Helix Labs

Attachment: helix_redline_v2.docx (Word, 82KB)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Ruiz <anna@helixlabs.com>
Date: 2026-12-13T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Fw: Draft order form and SLA — blackout windows & credits

Folks — forwarding Anna's annotated doc and ask. High level: Helix wants narrower "blackout" definition and a more granular credit ladder for partial region degradations. They also asked for a patch rollback SLA for emergency hotfixes during cutovers.

Initial thoughts: we can tighten scheduled maintenance window to a 2-hour weekday window with explicit notice timelines, but we should avoid absolute weekday prohibitions (impacts ops flexibility & capacity planning). For credit ladder, propose a three-tier regional degradation model (5-30 min, 30-180 min, >180 min) with scaled credits capped at X% per month — see attached spreadsheet draft.

Please review and propose concrete redline language by EOD Dec 15 so we can produce the order form redline for Anna before their Dec 19 procurement deadline. I'll pull in Legal's tracked changes after we have ops language.

Jonas
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: credit-ladder-spreadsheet.xlsx (Excel, 24KB)

Subject: Re: Fw: Draft order form and SLA — blackout windows & credits

Jonas / team,

I've sketched specific redline language for the MSA + Order Form. High-level legal positions:
- Scheduled maintenance: keep a baseline 4-hour weekly maintenance window for major platform upgrades but allow customers to opt into narrower, reserved windows in the order form. If Helix requests a committed 2-hour weekday window, we can accept that as a paid "Committed Maintenance Window" in the Order Form with a small premium.
- Blackout definition: we can replace the term "blackout" with "Unscheduled Service Interruption" and limit it to total service unavailability (not performance degradation). This reduces ambiguity.
- Credit ladder: propose a capped staircase expressed as % of monthly invoice per impacted region (see table). For partial-performance incidents we recommend credits tied to sustained latency degradations exceeding a defined threshold for N consecutive minutes.
- Emergency rollback SLA: ops can commit to initiating rollback within 60 minutes for emergency hotfixes during scheduled maintenance; full rollback completion windows depend on customer topology and will be included as an ops note rather than a strict SLA (too many variables).

I uploaded a tracked-changes PDF of the Order Form redline here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-helix-sla-redlines

If we want commercial flexibility, Kimberly and Marissa can propose optional order-form clauses (e.g., Committed Maintenance Window fee, Money-back cap increases for enterprise tiers).

Laura Bennett
Lead Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_orderform_redline.pdf (PDF, 38KB)

Date: 2026-12-16T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft order form and SLA — blackout windows & credits (Proposed compromise)

Anna — thanks for the quick review and the annotated copy. Attached is our proposed Order Form redline (proposed_orderform_redline.pdf) and the credit ladder spreadsheet. Summary of the compromise: 

- Scheduled maintenance: Redwood will reserve a default weekly 4-hour window for major platform upgrades, but we will add a customer-specific "Committed Maintenance Window" clause so Helix can lock a 2-hour weekday window for production with a nominal monthly fee.
- Blackout: replace with "Unscheduled Service Interruption" defined strictly as complete service unavailability for the tenant in the impacted region. Performance degradations will be handled under a separate "Performance Degradation" clause with latency thresholds and time-based triggers.
- Credit ladder: three tiers for regional incidents with clear minute thresholds and capped monthly credit exposure. See spreadsheet for exact percentages.
- Emergency rollback: Ops commits to initiating rollback within 60 minutes of incident classification, with progress updates every 15 minutes until resolved. Completion windows remain conditional and will be documented as operational expectations.

Next steps: 
1) Helix to confirm willingness to pay for the Committed Maintenance Window option (we can include a pricing line in the order form).
2) Legal teams to exchange final tracked changes — Laura will circulate a legal-only redline by EOD Dec 17.
3) If Helix confirms step 1 by Dec 18, we'll prepare DocuSign and target signature before Dec 22.

I've included a DocuSign placeholder: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/HXL-2026-45

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_orderform_redline.pdf; credit-ladder-spreadsheet.xlsx
